photos.caption: A view of Zanzibar. Wood engraving from Stanley's How I Found Livingstone, 1872.
Barghash bin Said, Sultan of Zanzibar 1870–1888 — ruler at the time of Stanley's arrival on 6 January 1871.
Henry Morton Stanley, journalist of the New York Herald, dispatched in 1871 to find Livingstone.
Discomforts of African travel — the Makata Swamp. Wood engraving from Stanley's How I Found Livingstone, 1872.
Making the most of a halt. Wood engraving from Stanley's How I Found Livingstone, 1872.
We attack Mirambo. Wood engraving from Stanley's How I Found Livingstone, 1872 — the Arab–Nyamwezi assault on Mirambo's stronghold.
Mtyela Kasanda, known as Mirambo — the Nyamwezi warlord whose blockade of the central caravan route forced Stanley to detour through Ukawendi.
David Livingstone, missionary and explorer (1813–1873). Carbon print of a photograph by Thomas Annan.
photos.credit: Thomas Annan / National Galleries of Scotland
